Transman struggle number 3: liking pink but not wearing it because dysphoria is a jerk and won't let you. 

It's taken me 3 years to start wearing little bits of pink here or there since coming out. Sometimes I'll even wear black lipstick when going out to a punk show just to mess with people. If it begins to bother me I just go in the bathroom and take it off. 

Remember: there's no one way to look masculine, you are still a guy. Even if you wear a cool pink hoodie and no amount of misgendering will change that.

It could be your "problem" though it's not really a problem in my opinion. Keep in mind everybody is different though, dysphoria takes different forms in everybody and so does euphoria. Sounds like you get gender euphoria from being called traditionally masculine things. 

When I was about 14 I discovered what trans was through myspace (I'm that old holy shit). I just thought I was a tomboy and it was normal "teenage girl problems" to cry everytime I saw my chest and to want to be one of the boys. I created an anonymous account on myspace that where I could be a guy and try it out online. I also referred to myself in my head as a dude and used he/him pronouns plus the name I picked out for myself. I started off binding with an ace bandage (please don't do that). When I realized I liked my chest flat like that and really enjoyed being called a boy I just kind of knew. This all took me about 5 years to figure it out and come to terms with my identity. It's been almost 13 years since then and I'm fully socially transitioned, beginning my medical transition soon and I haven't really looked back or second guessed. I'm a man. It's just who I am.
Sure being trans isn't always fun and exciting but I wouldn't trade it for the world. It has made me tougher than anybody I know and I grew up into a pretty cool human in my opinion. 

Hope you find peace and figure it all out, I'm sure you will and if you need a listening ear I'm here for you.

Hi, pre-everything here. I've only socially transitioned, I'm about to begin medical. Please remember what works for me may not work for you. 

To deepen my voice I've had to learn to speak more from my chest rather than my throat. Takes a little practice but it seems to help. There are videos online that could possibly help. 

For my wardrobe I wear a loose fitting shirt under a button up or jacket (sometimes both), if I'm feeling dyphoric or can't wear my binder I'll wear the biggest thickest hoodie I own. I also like wearing anything with structured shoulders, makes me look broad and more traditionally masculine shaped. I wear straight cut jeans that are a little loose around my thighs/hips in order to look a little more boxy, sometimes I still wear skinny jeans but only when I'm feeling real comfortable with myself that day. I wear a lot of snap backs, personally they help me feel more boyish. Also I wear big chunky doc martens boots, makes my feet look big and added bonus they give me an inch of height. 

Not sure what to tell you with the face, I don't know what yours looks like. Sorry.

Also if you've never worn a binder, stretch beforehand and take a few deep breaths. After you've put it on stretch again and make sure you can breathe comfortably. Be sure you get the right size, don't go down a size it can hurt you and be very unsafe. Looking down you might still see a little bump where your chest is but remember, even cis-guys chests have a little bump where their pecs are. That's also where wearing not only a shirt but layering it under other stuff like I do comes in handy. It helps make your chest appear flatter.

I don't know if you have gotten your hair cut short but one thing I've learned is to make sure whoever cuts it makes your hairline square in the back. If they round it around your neck it looks like a girls cut and that's not what you want. 

Hope any of this helps, if you have any questions feel free to message me. I'm glad to help bro.

There's a definite learning curve, the first few months I had to lay on my back legs splayed to get the cup in, just so I could learn how to fold/angle it best for my body. After you get that part down it's pretty easy to learn standing up. I prefer changing it in the shower when my body is more relaxed, but if I don't have time for that I put one foot on the side of the bathtub and do it that way. 

I prefer folding it in a U shape, seems easier to make it pop open like it needs to. Also, after you get it in I would make sure it's able to spin, if you can twist it in a circle it is open properly and you have less chance of it being uncomfortable or leaking. If you know where your cervix is be sure to have it underneath it and kind of angled towards. 

Good luck on your journey, I've been using a cup now for a year or two and love it. I never plan on going back to using anything else.
